jurisdictions.name: Scarborough
notes: A pool permit is required for any swimming or wading pool more than 24 inches deep, including seasonal pools. Pools must meet the zoning district setbacks.
The submittal list includes proof of title or interest, the pool permit application, a site plan, a scaled pool drawing with dimensions and manufacturer information.
Plans can be emailed to SUBMITTALS@SCARBOROUGHMAINE.ORG. An electrical permit application is required with the pool application.
In-ground pools require fencing. Inspections and the fence or safety barrier must be in place before the pool is used.

jurisdictions.name: South Portland
jurisdictions.office: City of South Portland Planning & Development, Code Enforcement
notes: The city has a Swimming Pool Permit Application. Applications can go through its online portal, by email to code@southportland.gov, or in person.
The application asks for a Class A or at least a Class D survey, a plot plan showing existing fences or walls, and a drainage plan meeting Sec. 27-1536(3) of the city code.
The application states fences must be 4 to 6 feet high with self-closing, self-latching devices.

Under Sec. 25-8, pool location is staked by a Maine-licensed surveyor or similar professional and verified before final inspection. Setbacks include 50 ft from the street and 10 ft from side or rear lines in residential districts.

sources.title: Swimming Pool Permit Application (City of South Portland)
Applications & Information (City of South Portland Code Enforcement)

state_level.note: Maine law (22 M.R.S. section 1632) requires a fence around every swimming pool, except portable above-ground pools with sidewalls at least 24 inches high. A house or accessory building can form part of the enclosure, and gates and doors must be securely fastenable.

source.title: Title 22, section 1632: Enclosure of swimming pool required
